goal: Make one Batch Authorization span the work it authorizes: derive its expiry from the authorized budget deadline on both Hosts instead of a hardcoded ten minutes, without relaxing any fail-closed clock, issuance, or renewal check.

acceptance.assertion: Batch authorization expiry is derived from the authorized budget.deadline_at on both Hosts, replacing the hardcoded now + 10 minutes in runtime/claude/kernel_ports.ts and .pi-extension/imm-unattended-batch.ts. The value bound at issuance is the one the literal user confirmed; no new default deadline is introduced and the existing default budget is unchanged.

Every existing fail-closed check in runtime/kernel/batch_authority.ts is preserved verbatim in effect: expiry and deadline must both be strictly in the future at issuance, an unreadable or non-monotonic clock still fails closed, and an expired authorization still refuses the batch and still requires a strictly newer literal-user confirmation to renew.

The renewal path in runtime/unattended/batch_runner.ts is retained, because a batch can still outlive a deadline the user themselves chose; a batch parked on a foreground Review inside its confirmed budget no longer expires, while one that passes its confirmed deadline still does.
